body:
Global crypto markets closed Saturday on a soft note, with total market capitalization sitting at $2.9T after a 24-hour drawdown of 3.08% that contrasted sharply with the constructive week-to-date picture. Volume came in at $88.4B across the space, healthy enough to suggest the selling was orderly rather than panicked, and BTC dominance ticked up to 58.3% as capital rotated defensively into the largest asset. The Fear and Greed index printed 74 today versus 71 yesterday, a modest uptick that tells you the broader sentiment remains firmly in greed territory even as prices leaked lower intraday — a classic late-week consolidation pattern where spot supply slightly overwhelms but conviction sellers are absent.

BTC held $84,161 at the close, down just 0.51% on the 24-hour window against $27.79B in volume, and the flatness of the 1-hour read at essentially 0.00% suggests price has found near-term equilibrium rather than breaking in either direction. The weekly performance of +3.64% frames today's drift as noise within a constructive trend. The level to watch on the downside is the psychological $83,000 zone; a clean hold there keeps the weekly structure intact. On the upside, any push with conviction through the mid-to-high $85,000s would shift short-term momentum firmly bullish and put the next band of resistance in focus. A separate CoinDesk report on Bitcoin potentially gaining Zcash-style shielded privacy through a layer-level implementation — without a consensus rule change — is worth tracking for longer-dated institutional sentiment around on-chain privacy compliance.

ETH was the clear underperformer among the large caps at $2,689.04, shedding 1.07% over 24 hours on $10.59B in volume, and at +1.93% on the week it continues to lag BTC's +3.64% — a divergence that reinforces the dominance narrative. XRP was the single worst performer tracked today at -3.15%, landing at $1.55, and the headline context is not friendly: the XRP Ledger's Batch upgrade has slipped to October 9 after validator support resets, a minor but real credibility friction point. The weekly gain of +9.12% means the holders are still comfortably in profit, but momentum is clearly fading. On the other side of the ledger, AVAX was the standout with a 24-hour gain of +3.20% to $10.94 and a week-to-date rip of +19.69%, the strongest weekly performer in the ZIMR tracked universe. ADA followed at +14.42% weekly and LINK at +14.02% — both holding those gains with ADA at $0.257074 and LINK at $14.27. Solana printed a quiet but positive +0.32% session at $121.28 and its technical story got a boost from a CoinDesk report that its 150-millisecond settlement upgrade has now reached a second public testnet, which is a meaningful execution milestone that the market has not yet fully priced.

The macro backdrop is tilted toward regulatory uncertainty rather than rate anxiety today. The most significant personnel story is the imminent departure of SEC Commissioner Hester Peirce, known as "Crypto Mom," who leaves her post on October 2. Peirce has been the most consistently crypto-friendly voice inside the SEC, and her exit removes a reliable institutional ally at a moment when the regulatory framework for digital assets in the US remains unsettled. That headline, combined with the news that the ex-CFTC leader is departing the Blockchain Association following the failure of the CLARITY vote, signals that Washington's crypto legislative push is losing momentum and key advocates simultaneously. The CFTC's $950M lawsuit against Cash FX for an alleged crypto-linked forex scheme adds another layer of enforcement noise that tends to suppress retail confidence at the margin. Tether's statement that it had "limited" exposure to a bank linked to an $84M US seizure is the kind of disclosure that the market absorbs without panic but files under ongoing counterparty risk monitoring.

Looking ahead, the October 9 XRP Ledger Batch upgrade rescheduling is the nearest hard catalyst — validator consensus dynamics around that date will determine whether XRP reclaims weekly momentum or continues to bleed against the pack. Hester Peirce's October 2 departure is a low-volatility but high-importance regulatory signal; watch for any commentary from remaining commissioners in the days immediately following that could shift the SEC's tone on pending crypto rulemaking. Solana's testnet progress on sub-200-millisecond settlement is the most credible positive technical catalyst in the near term and could drive SOL outperformance if the second testnet clears without incident. The broader risk to the constructive weekly setup is a BTC break below $83,000 on meaningful volume, which would invite deleveraging across altcoins that have run 10-20% in 7 days and have little technical support directly beneath them. Fear and Greed at 74 with prices fading intraday is not a red flag, but it is a reminder that sentiment is not cheap — any macro shock landing over the weekend could reset the tape quickly.
